title: Agent Skills specification
notes: Open SKILL.md format specification. Verified constraints: a skill is a directory containing at minimum a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown content; name is required, 1-64 characters, lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, must match the parent directory name; description is required, 1-1024 characters, describing what the skill does and when to use it; optional fields are license, compatibility (max 500 characters), metadata (string-to-string map), and allowed-tools (experimental). Progressive disclosure guidance: SKILL.md body under 5000 tokens recommended, main SKILL.md under 500 lines; file references use relative paths from the skill root.

title: Claude Code documentation - Agent Skills
notes: Official Claude Code skills documentation. A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter (name, description) plus a Markdown instruction body. Verified 2026-10-03.

title: Codex documentation - Building skills
notes: Official Codex skills documentation (developers.openai.com/codex/skills currently resolves to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills). Verified: a skill is a directory with a SKILL.md file plus optional scripts and references; SKILL.md must include name and description. Documented discovery locations: repository-level $CWD/.agents/skills (also parent directories up to the repository root), user-level $HOME/.agents/skills, admin /etc/codex/skills, plus skills bundled with Codex. Optional interface metadata (display_name, short_description, icons, brand_color, default_prompt), a policy.allow_implicit_invocation flag, and MCP tool dependencies live in agents/openai.yaml, not SKILL.md frontmatter. Skills can be disabled without deletion via [[skills.config]] entries in ~/.codex/config.toml.

title: Cursor documentation - Skills
notes: Official Cursor skills documentation. Verified: each skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file with optional scripts/, references/, assets/ directories. Documented discovery locations: project-level .agents/skills/ and .cursor/skills/, user-level ~/.agents/skills/ and ~/.cursor/skills/, plus compatibility loading from .claude/skills/ and .codex/skills/ (and their user-level equivalents); skills inside nested project subdirectories are also discovered. Frontmatter: name (required, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens, must match the parent folder name) and description (required, used by the agent to determine relevance); Cursor-specific optional keys are paths (glob patterns scoping activation; legacy globs still accepted), disable-model-invocation (explicit /skill-name invocation only), icon, color, and metadata (arbitrary string-to-string map).

title: Gemini CLI documentation - Agent Skills
notes: Official Gemini CLI skills documentation (overview at /docs/cli/skills/, authoring at /docs/cli/creating-skills/). Verified: SKILL.md is the only required component; scripts/, references/, assets/ are optional. Documented discovery locations (lowest to highest precedence): built-in skills bundled with the CLI, extension skills, user skills in ~/.gemini/skills/ or the ~/.agents/skills/ alias, workspace skills in .gemini/skills/ or the .agents/skills/ alias. Frontmatter fields named by the docs: name (a unique identifier that should match the directory name) and description ('CRITICAL. This is how Gemini decides when to use the skill.').

title: OpenCode documentation - Skills
notes: Official OpenCode skills documentation. Verified: skills define reusable behavior via SKILL.md definitions loaded on demand through the native skill tool. Documented discovery locations: project .opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, global ~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, Claude-compatible .claude/skills/ and ~/.claude/skills/, and agent-compatible .agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/; project paths are resolved by walking up from the working directory to the git worktree. Only name (required) and description (required) plus license, compatibility, and metadata (optional) are recognized; unknown fields are ignored. Name must match ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, be 1-64 characters, and match the containing directory name; description must be 1-1024 characters.

title: Packsmith security baseline for Skill content
notes: Baseline pattern inventory defined by the Packsmith v0.2 implementation plan (section 11, Security): sensitive file access patterns (.env, credentials, private keys, ~/.ssh), remote shell execution patterns (curl | sh, wget | sh, remote executable scripts), and dangerous destructive shell patterns (sudo, rm -rf). These are Packsmith gate-policy checks, not claims made by any runtime vendor; they flag Skill content that a human should review before trusting it.
